texts.preamble: State Of Gujarat - Thro' D.T.Trivedi, ... vs Suresh K Shah - Thro' Atulkumar Kantilal ... on 8 August, 2025 R/Cr.A/1691/2013 Judgme In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad R/Criminal Appeal No. 1691 of 2013 (Against Acquittal) For Approval And Signature: Honourable Ms. Justice S.V. Pinto Sd/- =============================================================== Approved for Reporting Yes =============================================================== State Of Gujarat - Thro' D.T.Trivedi, Food Inspector Versus Suresh K Shah - Thro' Atulkumar Kantilal Shah - Partner & Ors. =============================================================== Appearance: Ms.C.M.Shah, App for the Appellant(s) No. 1 Mr Dk Modi(1317) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 2 Mr Jv Japee(358) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1 Mr Md Modi(1318) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 2 =============================================================== Coram:Honourable Ms. Justice S.V. Pinto Date : 08/08/2025 Oral Judgment
texts.facts: 1.1. The respondents hereinafter referred to as 'the accused' as they stood in the rank and file in the original case, for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity. 2. The relevant facts leading to filing of the present appeal are as under: 2.1. The complainant - Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi was a notified Food Inspector and on 09.10.1991 at around 13:15 hours, visited the shop of the accused no. 1 and gave his identity as a Food Inspector. The complainant purchased 450 grams of 'mustard oil' of 'Gopi Brand' from a packed tin and paid Rs.15.30 paisa and after the entire procedure was followed, the 450 grams of mustard oil was placed in equal proportions in three clean and dry glass jars. The glass jars were sealed and labeled and placed in brown paper and sealed and one sample was sent to the Public Analyst, Rajkot as per the procedure and the other two samples were sent to the Assistant Commissioner and Local Health Authority, Gandhinagar. The report of the Public Analyst was received, which showed that the sample did not conform to the standards and provisions laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, and after the permission for filing the complaint was received, the complaint was filed by the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined complainant Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi against the accused no.1 - the vendor, the accused no.2 - the wholesaler and the accused no.3 - the producer of the mustard oil. 2.2. The learned Trial Court was pleased to take cognizance of the offence and the summons were issued to the accused and the accused Nos. 1 and 2 were duly served with the summons and appeared before the learned Trial Court. During the trial before the learned Trial Court, the accused no. 3, who was the producer, could not be traced out and the complainant could not produce the new address of the accused no. 3 and non-bailable warrants were issued, but could not be served. 2.3. During the pendency of the trial, the complainant Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi expired on 23.05.1998 and the accused nos. 2 and 3 filed an application at Exh.38 stating that as the complainant has expired, the complaint may be dismissed under the provision of 256 of the Cr.P.C. and they may be acquitted from the offence under the Food Adulteration Act as it is mandatory for the complainant to prove the case. In support of their say, they have produced the copy of the death certificate of the complainant at Exh.45 and on perusal of the same, it transpires that the complainant Mr.Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi has expired on 23.05.1998. Subsequently, the application was withdrawn. Thereafter, the death certificate of the complainant was produced on record and the learned Trial Court was pleased to pass the impugned order, and hence, the present appeal may be dismissed. 6.1.
texts.arguments: 3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned order passed by the learned Trial Court, the appellant - State has filed the present appeal mainly stating that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court is contrary to law and evidence on record. The learned Trial Court has passed the impugned order of acquittal without giving any cogent and convincing reasons and the same is illegal, invalid and improper, and therefore, the same requires to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 5. Learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State has submitted that the non availability of the original Food Inspector, who had collected the sample, on account of his unfortunate demise, cannot be a circumstance to defeat the prosecution case so as to allow the accused to escape liability, particularly when the report of the Public Analyst on record clearly establishes that the sample of the food article was not in conformity with the standards prescribed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules. Learned APP further submits that the documentary evidence on record unerringly demonstrates that all mandatory requirements under the Prevention Food Adulteration Act and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules were duly complied with, and therefore, the accused was liable to be convicted and punished in accordance with law. Learned APP has urged this Court to quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order of acquittal and to find the accused guilty for the said offence and impose maximum sentence on the accused. 6. Learned advocate Mr.M.D.Modi for the respondents submits that as per the case of the Food Inspector, the sample was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined collected on 09.10.1991 and the report of the Public Analyst is dated 11.11.1991 and the sanction to file the case is dated 29.02.1996 and the Food Inspector filed the complaint on 20.04.1996. 1. State of Gujarat Vs. Ashokkumar Aasandas Kotak and Anr. reported in 2007(2) FAC 50. 2. State of Gujarat Vs. Bharatkumar Keshavlal Bhatt (Seller) reported in 2010(0) GLHEL-HC 226132. [ 7. On perusal of the entire record of the case, it appears that in the present case that the original complainant - Food Inspector, Mr.Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi, who had collected the sample, who was the principal witness to the alleged offence, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined expired during the pendency of the proceedings.
